endorsements.quote: AI outputs must function as decision-support mechanisms rather than autonomous determinants of care.
Explicit human-in-the-loop oversight and override mechanisms, particularly for outputs influencing diagnostic thresholds, treatment prioritization, or public communication.
Red-team exercises must simulate high-risk, ethically ambiguous, and culturally sensitive scenarios, with documented review of system responses and escalation pathways.
Safety monitoring should include adverse-event reporting rates, override frequency tracking, and systematic review of escalation triggers in ethically sensitive cases.

Transparent patient communication is likewise essential; where algorithmic reasoning influences treatment options, it must be explainable in conceptually intelligible terms that preserve trust and autonomy.

To operationalize HP beyond general safety claims, we suggest introducing a Psychiatry-Specific Harm Taxonomy that defines the minimum domains against which AI systems must be stress-tested prior to guideline integration.
The format and complexity of explanations are calibrated to the intended audience (clinician, policymaker, regulator, or patient representative).
Escalation protocols for ethically sensitive or high-risk outputs, preventing automated propagation of potentially harmful recommendations.
A transparent description of model inputs, training data, interpretive assumptions, and known limitations is publicly accessible.

unlisted_practices: Require a mean explainability score threshold; systems scoring below it must not be endorsed regardless of predictive performance.
Provide validated post hoc interpretability mechanisms when performance gains come at the cost of reduced model transparency before adoption.
Log deliberative processes, including expert disagreement and patient-representative input, when AI-generated content informs final recommendations.
Continuously manage model drift and domain shift through an open, continuously updating pipeline with periodic re-evaluation.
Intentionally include underrepresented groups such as refugees and conflict-affected populations in AI training data to reduce bias.
Adapt AI implementation to infrastructural capacity using tiered models while keeping accountability and bias safeguards constant.
Monitor fairness using subgroup performance metrics, calibration analyses, and bias-detection procedures across demographic, linguistic, and cultural strata.
Evaluate AI's impact on trust, therapeutic alliance, and patient autonomy using validated instruments, not only predictive accuracy.

screen.reason: This paper presents a conceptual/guideline framework proposing responsible AI integration principles (explainability, shared decision-making, EHR integration, harm prevention) for psychiatry rather than an empirical study.
